lines: # Advertising built on research, testing, and honest reporting — not guesswork.
I'm Talha, a digital marketer focused on Google Ads and Meta Ads. DigitalTalha is my personal brand — where I put in the work to understand a business before I ever build a campaign for it.
Image: Talha Alam, digital marketer and founder of DigitalTalha

DigitalTalha isn't an agency — it's me. I'm a digital marketer currently pursuing my BBA at Amity University, and I focus specifically on Google Ads and Meta Ads because that's where I've chosen to build real depth rather than spread myself thin.
Building DigitalTalha is how I'm turning that focus into a professional identity — one built on the work I actually do, not on claims I haven't earned yet.
* Approach Research first, test constantly, report honestly
* Working style Solo — you work directly with me, always
## How I got into digital marketing
### A first spark, back in Class 12
My interest in marketing started with something I came across online during Class 12. It was a small spark, but it was enough to send me looking for more.
### Reading my way into the subject

I started reading blogs, watching YouTube content, and picking up books on marketing — including Philip Kotler's Marketing Management and Seth Godin's work. The more I read, the more I gravitated toward digital marketing specifically, since that's where businesses and customers increasingly meet.
### Choosing a real course over scattered content

I didn't want to learn digital marketing as a set of disconnected topics, so I researched several courses before enrolling. I chose the UT Digital Media course by Umar Tazkeer, a structured three-month program that gave me a proper foundation.

After the course, I kept practicing — keyword and audience research, Google Ads and Meta Ads campaign structure, ad copywriting, conversion tracking with GA4 and GTM, budget planning, and A/B testing. I've worked through the process of planning a campaign and building an advertising strategy end to end, treating it as real practice rather than a box to check.
### Building a name around the work
DigitalTalha is where that practice turns into a professional identity. It's still early — but it's built to grow with real client work, not around claims that aren't true yet.
## Two channels, done properly — not ten, done poorly
I've deliberately kept my focus narrow so I can go deep instead of wide.
Understanding intent, keyword research, campaign structure, targeting, tracking, and ongoing optimization — built around what a searcher is actually trying to do.
Reaching relevant audiences across Meta's ecosystem through audience research, creative testing, messaging, and structured optimization.
The goal was never clicks or impressions on their own — it's understanding whether advertising is actually moving a business toward a real outcome.
## Advertising should explain a solution — not force a sale
Good advertising isn't about pushing people toward a purchase. It's about helping a business communicate the right solution to the right people — clearly enough that the value is easy to see.

Before I write a single ad, I want to know who the audience is, what problem they actually have, what they care about, and why they'd choose this solution over another. Everything else is built on top of that.
I also treat advertising as ongoing, not a one-time launch. Behavior, markets, and competitors keep changing — so a message that works today won't necessarily work forever.
That's why I run every campaign through the same loop, and why I'd rather tell you honestly what isn't working than dress it up.
This is the sequence I follow on every campaign — a working approach, not a guarantee of a specific result.
Get clear on the business, the offer, the audience, and the actual objective before anything else.
Study customers, competitors, keywords, and the wider market context that shapes the campaign.
Put together the campaign structure — messaging, targeting, creatives, and tracking, from the start.
Watch the performance data that actually matters, not vanity metrics that look good but say little.
Test variables deliberately instead of assuming the first approach is the right one.
Use what the data shows to make the next version of the campaign better than the last.
## Practical skills I've built and applied
These are areas I've studied and put into practice directly — no inflated numbers, just the real list.
This list reflects real, hands-on practice — not a certification or a client results claim. I'll update this page as that changes.
## The foundation for a career in performance marketing

I built DigitalTalha to give my work a name and a home. It's my professional identity — the place where research, testing, and honest advertising come together, and where I hold myself to it publicly.
I'm also building a presence on Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn alongside it. None of this is about looking established before I am — it's about growing through real work, one campaign at a time.
→ A name built alongside the work, not ahead of it
→ A long-term goal: becoming one of the best performance marketers I can be
→ Continuous learning in data, testing, and consumer behavior
## How I work with the people I work with
No unnecessary jargon or hiding behind complicated marketing language — just a straight explanation of what's happening and why.
I take the time to understand your business and audience before making any advertising decisions.
Decisions are backed by data and structured experiments, not assumptions about what should work.
I'll tell you honestly what's working, what isn't, and what needs to change — no dressing up weak performance.
Every campaign is something to learn from. I treat optimization as ongoing, not a one-time setup.
DigitalTalha is a solo, personal brand. When you work with me, you work directly with me — always.
If you're thinking through your next step with Google Ads or Meta Ads, I'd like to hear about your business and what you're trying to achieve.
Performance marketing that drives more leads, sales, and measurable growth.

lines: # Meta Lead Campaign — From Start to Finish
This is a hypothetical brand that I created and used to build a complete Meta lead-generation campaign from start to finish.
The purpose of this project is to understand how the major parts of a campaign work together:
Business Goal → Lead Collection → Landing Page → Tracking → Campaign Setup → Audience → Creative → Lead → Remarketing → Customer → Optimization
For this example, imagine a business selling a service for ₹799 and using Meta Ads to generate leads through a website.
Before creating an ad, we need to decide what the business actually wants.
A lead is someone who shows interest and provides information such as their name, phone number, or email address so the business can follow up.
Meta Ad → Lead → Sales Follow-up → Customer
The campaign should therefore be built around generating valuable leads, not simply clicks or impressions.
# 2. Choose How to Collect the Lead
Meta’s Leads objective can be used with different lead-collection methods. Two common options are:
The form opens directly inside Facebook or Instagram.
The user clicks the ad, visits the website, and submits a form.
For this project, we choose the landing page.

Instant Forms create less friction and can produce more submissions, sometimes at a lower cost per lead. However, the low-friction process can also result in people submitting their information with less consideration.
A landing page adds another step:
Click → Read → Understand Offer → Submit Form
That extra effort may reduce volume, but it can also help qualify interest and give the business more control over the conversion experience.
Offer + Audience + Creative + Landing Page + Form + Lead Quality + Sales Process
A landing page is a webpage designed around one main marketing objective.
A good lead-generation page should clearly communicate:
The page should also contain appropriate privacy and legal information.
Ad creates interest → Landing page explains the offer → Form captures the lead
The message should remain consistent from the ad to the page.
Once the landing page is ready, we need to measure what happens after the ad click.
* Which campaign or creative produced the lead?
* What happened after the lead was generated?
GTM + Data Layer + GA4 + Meta Pixel + Meta CAPI + UTM Parameters
Each tool has a different role.
GTM is a tag management system.
It helps us manage tracking instructions and decide when they should fire.
Trigger → when the instruction should fire
Variable → information used by the tag or trigger
Data Layer → structured information passed from the website to GTM
GTM manages tracking; it does not replace GA4 or Meta.
Our landing-page form uses AJAX, meaning the form can submit without reloading the page.
That creates a problem if we try to track conversion through a thank-you page.
Instead, after a successful submission, the website can push a custom event such as:
GA4 and Meta receive the conversion
This is more reliable than treating a button click as a completed lead.
GA4 helps us understand what people do on the website.
A simple way to remember it:
The Meta Pixel is browser-side tracking.
It sends relevant website events to Meta, such as a Lead event after a successful form submission.
Its purpose includes helping Meta measure and optimize advertising performance.
Conversions API (CAPI) provides another route for sending events to Meta, typically from a server or other controlled environment.
Browser tracking can be affected by privacy restrictions, ad blockers, cookie limitations, and other technical factors. CAPI can provide another path for sending important conversion events.
It does not give Meta automatic access to everything on the server. Only configured and permitted information is sent.
Using both gives Meta multiple ways to receive the same conversion information.
However, the same real conversion must not be counted twice.
Meta should recognize these as the same conversion, not two leads.
This is why proper event deduplication is important.
## How Can Meta Tracking Be Implemented?
Meta tracking can be implemented through:
A plugin is simply one implementation method.
We should track meaningful actions rather than everything possible.
Page View → visitor loads the page
CTA Click → visitor clicks the main button
Form Start → visitor begins the form
Lead → visitor successfully submits the form
Before launching the campaign, test the complete journey.
Check whether tags, triggers, variables, and data-layer events are working.
Check whether website activity and the Lead event are being received.
Check whether Pixel and CAPI events are arriving and being properly deduplicated.
Open page → Click CTA → Submit form → Generate Lead event → Verify GA4 → Verify Meta
Only after this should we launch the campaign.
UTM parameters add campaign information to the landing-page URL.
Pixel/CAPI → send conversion information to Meta
UTMs → add campaign context to website traffic and analytics
Consistency matters. Use a clear naming convention rather than changing values randomly.
Once the landing page and tracking are ready, we move to Meta Ads Manager.
Meta can be understood at three levels:
What do we want to achieve?
Who should we reach, when, and where?
because the business wants to generate leads.
because the lead is collected on our landing page.
because a successful form submission is the actual business conversion.
> More leads do not automatically mean better leads.
Lead quality must eventually be measured through the sales process.
Bid strategy affects how Meta competes in the auction while trying to achieve the campaign goal.
The exact options can change, so the principle is more important than memorizing a specific label.
A campaign should run long enough to collect meaningful data.
The appropriate evaluation period depends on budget, conversion volume and campaign conditions.
For this example, we can start with:
Broad targeting means we are giving Meta room to find likely converters instead of heavily restricting delivery with interest filters.
This does not mean we do not understand the customer.
It means we are allowing the platform’s delivery system to do more of the audience selection.
Placements determine where the ad can appear.
For this project, we can consider Facebook and Instagram placements.
However, this should not be treated as a universal best practice. Automated placement options may also be appropriate depending on the campaign, creative and performance data.
At the ad level, we choose:
A partnership ad is not necessary because this is a standard business advertisement.
# 12. Build the Creative Around a Reason to Buy
Customer Problem → Angle → Message → Visual → CTA
Focus on the customer’s current difficulty.
Focus on the result they want.
Focus on saving time or effort.
Focus on the value of the offer.
The same product can be marketed from several angles because different people can want the same product for different reasons.
For this campaign, we could create four image creatives:
The purpose is not simply to have more ads.
It is to test different reasons for buying.
When using AI to create these visuals, provide useful context such as:
Customer photos and testimonials can also be useful when the business has the appropriate rights and permissions.
The main body of the ad.
The action we want the user to take.
The ad promise must match the landing page.
Landing page: clearly provides that consultation
This creates a consistent path from ad to conversion.
Not everyone will become a lead during the first visit.
Some of the remaining visitors may still be valuable prospects.
Where eligible, we can create audiences from previous interactions and show them relevant follow-up advertising.
A Custom Audience is a defined audience created from eligible customer or interaction data.
A Saved Audience is a reusable targeting configuration.
A Lookalike Audience helps find new people similar to a source audience.
Existing Customers → Lookalike → New Potential Customers
Lookalike = new people similar to a source
A Lookalike is not simply a way to reach the same people again.
# 16. Think About Audiences as a Funnel
We can divide the audience into:
Different stages can require different messages.
Existing customers may also be excluded from prospecting campaigns where appropriate.
After launch, look at the entire funnel:
Impression → Click → Landing Page View → Form Start → Lead → Qualified Lead → Customer → Revenue
* Impressions — how often ads were shown
* Reach — how many people saw them
* Landing Page Views — people who successfully loaded the page
* Lead Quality — how valuable the leads are
* Customer Conversion Rate — how many leads become customers
* Customer Acquisition Cost — cost to acquire a customer
# 18. Don’t Judge the Campaign by One Metric
Campaign B may be far more valuable.
> Cheap leads are not necessarily better leads.
A high CTR with very few leads may indicate a problem with:
Testing means deliberately changing something to learn what improves performance.
Landing Page A vs Landing Page B
Changing audience, budget, creative, placement and landing page all at once makes it difficult to know what caused the result.
Track → Analyze → Decide → Change → Measure Again
A creative can become less effective when people repeatedly see it.
When a meaningful pattern appears, new creative angles may be needed.
The important word is meaningful. Do not react to tiny amounts of data.
# 22. The Complete Campaign in One Flow
For our ₹799 service, the complete process is:
Choose Website Instead of Instant Form
Track AJAX Form With a `generate_lead` Data-Layer Event
A Meta lead-generation campaign is not simply:
Business Goal + Offer + Audience + Creative + Landing Page + Tracking + Sales + Optimization
A great creative cannot fix a weak offer.
A great offer cannot fix a broken landing page.
A good landing page cannot fix broken tracking.
Correct tracking cannot compensate for poor campaign strategy.
And generating a large number of leads does not automatically mean the campaign is successful.
> Generate valuable customers at a cost the business can sustainably afford.
That is what the entire campaign is designed to achieve.
Performance marketing that drives more leads, sales, and measurable growth.
